source_records.abstract: Temporal networks have gained significant prominence in the past decade for modelling dynamic interactions within complex systems. A key challenge in this domain is Temporal Link Prediction (TLP), which aims to forecast future connections by analysing historical network structures across a range of applications. While existing surveys have addressed specific aspects of TLP, they typically lack a comprehensive framework that distinguishes between representation and inference methods, the two key ingredients of TLP. This survey bridges this gap by introducing a novel taxonomy that explicitly examines representation and inference in existing methods, providing a novel classification of approaches for TLP. We analyse how different representation techniques capture temporal and structural dynamics, examining their compatibility with various inference methods for link prediction tasks. Our taxonomy not only clarifies the methodological landscape but also reveals promising unexplored combinations of existing techniques. This taxonomy provides a systematic foundation for tackling emerging challenges in TLP, including model explainability and scalable architectures for complex temporal networks.

source_records.abstract: Early detection of heart disorders relies heavily on identifying abnormalities in electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, yet most deep learning methods depend on large annotated datasets, which are difficult to obtain in practice. We present a combined unsupervised framework that leverages the advantages of both Transformers and LSTMs for reconstruction-based anomaly detection. The model is trained only on normal ECG recordings, enabling it to learn the underlying rhythm of healthy cardiac activity. At inference, irregular beats stand out through higher reconstruction errors, separated by a simple threshold. On benchmark datasets, the framework shows strong generalization – achieving 96.67% accuracy on ECG5000 and 96.44% accuracy on MIT-BIH. In our design, we have a lead-specific strategy for PTB-XL where separate models are trained per lead to maintain the small morphological differences, rather than averaging signals. Overall, our proposed method provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ECG anomaly detection alternatives that we hope will provide a valuable tool for automated monitoring and early screening of arrhythmias.

source_records.abstract: Generative deep learning models have demonstrated strong performance in data generation tasks; graph-based variants extend this capability by exploiting the relational structure of the data, which is explicitly encoded as a graph. However, graph deep learning approaches, such as variational graph autoencoders (VGAEs), often suffer from oversmoothing, which degrades the quality of generated representations. While oversmoothing has been studied in large-scale graph settings, its impact under low sensor (i.e., sparsely connected graph) density remains largely unexplored. In this work, we propose the Mean-Field Variational Graph Autoencoder (MFVGAE) which integrates a smoothing operation based on mean-field layers with VGAEs. This refinement improves embedding quality by regularizing latent representations, enhancing local discriminative power in graph-based VAEs while constraining oversmoothing. We evaluate MFVGAE on a data generation task, posed as a matrix completion problem, using real-world electromagnetic and air quality exposure measurements collected in Belgium. Results show that MFVGAE outperforms other statistical and deep learning methods, including the standard VGAE, under two sparse and irregular real-world data conditions.

source_records.abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection is a crucial component of autonomous monitoring systems, where capturing informative representations to detect anomalies is of utmost importance. Deep learning approaches such as reconstruction-based autoencoders and variational autoencoders perform well on this task, but they typically overlook geometric and topological structure in the data while incurring high computational cost. In this paper, we introduce the use of topological features derived from persistence diagrams for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series. We propose a hybrid framework that combines these topological features with rich representations extracted from a trained sequence-to-sequence variational autoencoder, scored jointly by Isolation Forest. We demonstrate bidirectional complementarity: adding topological features to autoencoder features improves F1 by up to $$15.0\%$$ 15.0 % , while adding autoencoder features to topological features improves F1 by up to $$8.3\%$$ 8.3 % . Furthermore, we show that the optimal topological representation depends on channel characteristics, and that the use of persistence landscapes yields additional gains over only using scalar summary statistics.

source_records.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) represent the complex interplay of transcription factors, regulatory elements, and target genes that orchestrate cellular identity and function, playing a crucial role in the differentiation and maintenance of stem cells. This chapter provides an overview of experimental and computational methodologies for inferring GRNs, with particular emphasis on single-cell approaches. We first review key experimental techniques for detecting transcription factor binding sites, chromatin accessibility, and DNA motifs, alongside essential databases that support GRN reconstruction. We then introduce computational inference methods that can be categorized into four principal frameworks: correlation-based approaches, regression and machine learning models, probabilistic and deep learning methods, and integrative or message-passing frameworks. To illustrate practical application, we present a case study applying the pySCENIC workflow to a peripheral blood mononuclear cell single-cell RNA sequencing dataset from mouse, demonstrating how regulon-based analysis can reveal cell-type-specific regulatory programs. This chapter aims to serve as a practical guide for researchers seeking to understand and implement GRN inference methodologies in stem cell biology and related fields.

source_records.abstract: In the field of Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval (RSITR), introducing auxiliary tasks like position reconstruction is an effective strategy to boost fine-grained cross-modal alignment. However, existing multi-task learning methods mostly use fixed weights to jointly optimize the primary retrieval task and auxiliary reconstruction tasks, implicitly assuming stable supervision quality of each task throughout the training process. In remote sensing scenarios, auxiliary reconstruction tasks suffer from severe uncertainty and inherent noise caused by cloud occlusion, illumination variation, and sensor noise. Fitting these unreliable supervision signals with fixed weights will interfere with shared representation learning, damage the optimization stability of the primary task, and impair the model’s generalization and robustness. To address this issue, we propose B-PRCLIP, a Bayesian uncertainty-aware multi-task learning framework for RSITR. It reformulates multi-task joint optimization as a maximum likelihood estimation problem under the homoscedastic uncertainty assumption. By introducing learnable log-variance parameters for auxiliary tasks, it adaptively evaluates their supervision credibility and optimization difficulty, and dynamically adjusts their weights in the total loss. This method automatically mitigates the negative impact of unreliable reconstruction signals on the shared encoder, improves multi-task collaborative optimization stability, and guides the model to focus on robust cross-modal semantic alignment. Experiments on two public benchmarks RSICD and RSITMD show that our method maintains excellent retrieval accuracy on clean test sets, significantly improves training stability, and exhibits stronger anti-interference ability under noise perturbations, validating the effectiveness of the proposed uncertainty-aware weighting mechanism.

source_records.abstract: Contamination source isolation in water distribution networks (WDN) is critical for ensuring public health and safety. Traditional graph-based methods rely on the complete WDN topology, which becomes ineffective under sparse sensor placement due to limited observations. In this paper, we propose a novel sensor-only graph learning framework that leverages self-attention mechanisms to learn latent connections among sensor nodes directly from water quality measurements, eliminating the need for physical network topology. This approach enables effective message passing and feature aggregation using only the deployed sensors as graph nodes. Additionally, we introduce a contrastive learning objective to regularize the learned adjacency matrix, ensuring it captures contamination-relevant dependencies. Experiments on benchmark WDN datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing graph-based and transformer-based models in contamination source isolation accuracy while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. The code and datasets are available at: https://github.com/KIOS-Research/SCGNN .

source_records.abstract: Linear decoders for spiking populations typically use only the instantaneous filtered activity of each neuron and therefore do not fully exploit the temporal structure present in neural responses. We study a delay-augmented linear readout in which each neuron contributes several time-shifted copies of its activity, giving the decoder access to recent response history without introducing recurrence or nonlinear processing. To ensure a fair comparison, we keep the total number of decoder inputs fixed across conditions: when more delay taps are added per neuron, the number of neurons is reduced accordingly. On one-dimensional reconstruction of band-limited white-noise signals, we compare this approach with a baseline readout that uses current activity alone in populations of leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF (ALIF) neurons. Delay-augmented decoding improves accuracy under matched decoder dimensionality, with gains that depend on signal timescale and firing regime. The largest improvements occur for ALIF populations and reach nearly 40% relative MSE reduction in the best settings, while LIF populations show smaller and more regime-dependent benefits. These results show that fixed spike-transmission delays can improve decoding efficiency without recurrence or learned temporal dynamics.

A key challenge in this domain is Temporal Link Prediction (TLP), which aims to forecast future connections by analysing historical network structures across a range of applications. While existing surveys have addressed specific aspects of TLP, they typically lack a comprehensive framework that distinguishes between representation and inference methods, the two key ingredients of TLP. This survey bridges this gap by introducing a novel taxonomy that explicitly examines representation and inference in existing methods, providing a novel classification of approaches for TLP. We analyse how different representation techniques capture temporal and structural dynamics, examining their compatibility with various inference methods for link prediction tasks. Our taxonomy not only clarifies the methodological landscape but also reveals promising unexplored combinations of existing techniques. This taxonomy provides a systematic foundation for tackling emerging challenges in TLP, including model explainability and scalable architectures for complex temporal networks.

source_records.abstract: Early detection of heart disorders relies heavily on identifying abnormalities in electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, yet most deep learning methods depend on large annotated datasets, which are difficult to obtain in practice. We present a combined unsupervised framework that leverages the advantages of both Transformers and LSTMs for reconstruction-based anomaly detection. The model is trained only on normal ECG recordings, enabling it to learn the underlying rhythm of healthy cardiac activity. At inference, irregular beats stand out through higher reconstruction errors, separated by a simple threshold. On benchmark datasets, the framework shows strong generalization – achieving 96.67% accuracy on ECG5000 and 96.44% accuracy on MIT-BIH. In our design, we have a lead-specific strategy for PTB-XL where separate models are trained per lead to maintain the small morphological differences, rather than averaging signals. Overall, our proposed method provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ECG anomaly detection alternatives that we hope will provide a valuable tool for automated monitoring and early screening of arrhythmias.

source_records.abstract: Generative deep learning models have demonstrated strong performance in data generation tasks; graph-based variants extend this capability by exploiting the relational structure of the data, which is explicitly encoded as a graph. However, graph deep learning approaches, such as variational graph autoencoders (VGAEs), often suffer from oversmoothing, which degrades the quality of generated representations. While oversmoothing has been studied in large-scale graph settings, its impact under low sensor (i.e., sparsely connected graph) density remains largely unexplored. In this work, we propose the Mean-Field Variational Graph Autoencoder (MFVGAE) which integrates a smoothing operation based on mean-field layers with VGAEs. This refinement improves embedding quality by regularizing latent representations, enhancing local discriminative power in graph-based VAEs while constraining oversmoothing. We evaluate MFVGAE on a data generation task, posed as a matrix completion problem, using real-world electromagnetic and air quality exposure measurements collected in Belgium. Results show that MFVGAE outperforms other statistical and deep learning methods, including the standard VGAE, under two sparse and irregular real-world data conditions.

source_records.abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection is a crucial component of autonomous monitoring systems, where capturing informative representations to detect anomalies is of utmost importance. Deep learning approaches such as reconstruction-based autoencoders and variational autoencoders perform well on this task, but they typically overlook geometric and topological structure in the data while incurring high computational cost. In this paper, we introduce the use of topological features derived from persistence diagrams for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series. We propose a hybrid framework that combines these topological features with rich representations extracted from a trained sequence-to-sequence variational autoencoder, scored jointly by Isolation Forest. We demonstrate bidirectional complementarity: adding topological features to autoencoder features improves F1 by up to $$15.0\%$$ 15.0 % , while adding autoencoder features to topological features improves F1 by up to $$8.3\%$$ 8.3 % . Furthermore, we show that the optimal topological representation depends on channel characteristics, and that the use of persistence landscapes yields additional gains over only using scalar summary statistics.

source_records.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) represent the complex interplay of transcription factors, regulatory elements, and target genes that orchestrate cellular identity and function, playing a crucial role in the differentiation and maintenance of stem cells. This chapter provides an overview of experimental and computational methodologies for inferring GRNs, with particular emphasis on single-cell approaches. We first review key experimental techniques for detecting transcription factor binding sites, chromatin accessibility, and DNA motifs, alongside essential databases that support GRN reconstruction. We then introduce computational inference methods that can be categorized into four principal frameworks: correlation-based approaches, regression and machine learning models, probabilistic and deep learning methods, and integrative or message-passing frameworks. To illustrate practical application, we present a case study applying the pySCENIC workflow to a peripheral blood mononuclear cell single-cell RNA sequencing dataset from mouse, demonstrating how regulon-based analysis can reveal cell-type-specific regulatory programs. This chapter aims to serve as a practical guide for researchers seeking to understand and implement GRN inference methodologies in stem cell biology and related fields.

source_records.abstract: In the field of Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval (RSITR), introducing auxiliary tasks like position reconstruction is an effective strategy to boost fine-grained cross-modal alignment. However, existing multi-task learning methods mostly use fixed weights to jointly optimize the primary retrieval task and auxiliary reconstruction tasks, implicitly assuming stable supervision quality of each task throughout the training process. In remote sensing scenarios, auxiliary reconstruction tasks suffer from severe uncertainty and inherent noise caused by cloud occlusion, illumination variation, and sensor noise. Fitting these unreliable supervision signals with fixed weights will interfere with shared representation learning, damage the optimization stability of the primary task, and impair the model’s generalization and robustness. To address this issue, we propose B-PRCLIP, a Bayesian uncertainty-aware multi-task learning framework for RSITR. It reformulates multi-task joint optimization as a maximum likelihood estimation problem under the homoscedastic uncertainty assumption. By introducing learnable log-variance parameters for auxiliary tasks, it adaptively evaluates their supervision credibility and optimization difficulty, and dynamically adjusts their weights in the total loss. This method automatically mitigates the negative impact of unreliable reconstruction signals on the shared encoder, improves multi-task collaborative optimization stability, and guides the model to focus on robust cross-modal semantic alignment. Experiments on two public benchmarks RSICD and RSITMD show that our method maintains excellent retrieval accuracy on clean test sets, significantly improves training stability, and exhibits stronger anti-interference ability under noise perturbations, validating the effectiveness of the proposed uncertainty-aware weighting mechanism.

source_records.abstract: Contamination source isolation in water distribution networks (WDN) is critical for ensuring public health and safety. Traditional graph-based methods rely on the complete WDN topology, which becomes ineffective under sparse sensor placement due to limited observations. In this paper, we propose a novel sensor-only graph learning framework that leverages self-attention mechanisms to learn latent connections among sensor nodes directly from water quality measurements, eliminating the need for physical network topology. This approach enables effective message passing and feature aggregation using only the deployed sensors as graph nodes. Additionally, we introduce a contrastive learning objective to regularize the learned adjacency matrix, ensuring it captures contamination-relevant dependencies. Experiments on benchmark WDN datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing graph-based and transformer-based models in contamination source isolation accuracy while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. The code and datasets are available at: https://github.com/KIOS-Research/SCGNN .

source_records.abstract: Linear decoders for spiking populations typically use only the instantaneous filtered activity of each neuron and therefore do not fully exploit the temporal structure present in neural responses. We study a delay-augmented linear readout in which each neuron contributes several time-shifted copies of its activity, giving the decoder access to recent response history without introducing recurrence or nonlinear processing. To ensure a fair comparison, we keep the total number of decoder inputs fixed across conditions: when more delay taps are added per neuron, the number of neurons is reduced accordingly. On one-dimensional reconstruction of band-limited white-noise signals, we compare this approach with a baseline readout that uses current activity alone in populations of leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) and adaptive LIF (ALIF) neurons. Delay-augmented decoding improves accuracy under matched decoder dimensionality, with gains that depend on signal timescale and firing regime. The largest improvements occur for ALIF populations and reach nearly 40% relative MSE reduction in the best settings, while LIF populations show smaller and more regime-dependent benefits. These results show that fixed spike-transmission delays can improve decoding efficiency without recurrence or learned temporal dynamics.
